title: Giguère’s periodic system
creator: Paul A. Giguère
edition: Historical arrangement pictured in 1966, using current element names

sources.title: Paul A. Giguère, The “New Look” for the Periodic System
sources.citation: Chemistry in Canada 18 (12), 36–39, December 1966; figure on p. 37

sources.title: Giguère’s Periodic Table — Internet Database of Periodic Tables

geometry.coordinates: y is vertical; s and d wings lie in the xy plane, p and f in the yz plane. The s wing extends toward negative x; d toward positive x; p toward negative z; f toward positive z.
geometry.faceConvention: Each record is a single outward-facing plane at ±0.035 from the physical tile center. Rotate its local +z normal by the supplied XYZ Euler rotation. Paired front/back records represent different elements; do not add back-facing text to the same record.

notes: The dated placard on the model reads ©1965. The source article’s footer states December 1966. The catalogue uses 1965, whereas the repository cites the 1966 publication.
All three photographs on the original article’s figure page were inspected. The last labeled cell is 103, printed Lw. It is represented here as lawrencium (Lr), without adding subsequent elements.

The photographed design has empty lower-row panels for future elements. Seven wholly unlabelled tiles are provided separately as structural blanks. The tile bearing 103 has an unlabelled opposite face.
Helium is opposite hydrogen in the s wing, above beryllium. Lutetium and lawrencium occupy the first d-wing position; lanthanum and actinium begin the f wing.
The Grover Lab reconstruction helps explain the facing panels. Its additional modern elements are excluded, and its Pr entry opposite Fm is corrected to Pa (91) using the original photograph.
Cell proportions, spacing, and thickness are normalized for interactive display. Original printed masses, period markers, and blank title placards are not transcribed.
